subject.title: [Bug]: auth bookkeeping fallback save can revert rotated OpenAI OAuth refresh token (invalidates login)

question: Should auth/secops sponsor a narrow fix that removes full-store fallback writes from bookkeeping and hardens OAuth refresh CAS conflicts for rotated OpenAI credentials?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair changes persisted OAuth credential integrity behavior in security-owned auth paths and should not be queued without human ownership.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow auth-store fix
options.body: Remove stale full-store bookkeeping saves, keep credential writes locked, and add regression coverage for lock-failure and CAS-conflict token rotation races.

options.title: Broaden into an auth transaction refactor
options.body: Pause this issue until maintainers redesign the auth-profile transaction API so state and secret writes are separated consistently across callers.

options.title: Wait for live race proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not start implementation until a maintainer can reproduce the race with redacted live or Crabbox evidence.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow auth-store fix
recommendation.body: Remove stale full-store bookkeeping saves, keep credential writes locked, and add regression coverage for lock-failure and CAS-conflict token rotation races.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently reviewed and landed the related managed OpenAI OAuth fallback repair with live proof, making them the best visible routing candidate for this auth-provider decision.
